title: ASVS Auditor CI report
description: Output contract for the agent-asvs-ci skill. Versioned with the skill: additive changes are minor releases, field removals or meaning changes are major.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 UTC, taken from the system clock, never guessed.

asvs_level.description: The level the scan targeted. Violations at or below it decide the gate.

files_scanned.description: Count of files actually read. null when it cannot be determined. 0 is reserved for a scan that never ran, and pairs with `error`.

total_findings.description: Everything found after deduplication, including findings dropped by the 50-finding emit cap.

unverifiable_findings.description: Findings carrying not_verifiable_in_code. Exactly the gap between the two gate booleans.

root_causes.description: Distinct root_cause values across all findings, including any the emit cap dropped: the number of fixes, where the per-level counters are the number of requirements violated. Optional so that reports from before 3.3.0 still validate; the prompt always emits it.

findings_truncated.description: True only when the 50-finding emit cap dropped something. Deduplication does not set it.

pass.description: No verifiable violation at or below the target level. Gate on this unless unverified should mean unsafe.

pass_including_unverifiable.description: No violation at all at or below the target level, including controls that could not be checked from source.

error.description: Present only when the scan could not run properly.

id.description: Derived from content, never a sequence number: ASVS-<requirement>-<repo-relative path>-<line>.

asvs_requirement.description: Requirement ID, e.g. V1.2.4. A section-level ID such as V1.2 is permitted only as the documented fallback when the bundled requirement text is unreachable — inventing a requirement number is worse than citing the section.

finding_type.description: Optional. `absence` for a control that is missing; omitted or `presence` otherwise.

file.description: Repo-relative path that exists in the scanned tree. For an absence finding, where the control belongs.

column.description: Optional. Omitted unless known exactly; never estimated.

context.description: At most 5 lines of surrounding code.

not_verifiable_in_code.description: Optional, and omitted entirely unless true. Marks a control that may be enforced at a proxy, CDN, gateway, or in documentation. Excluded from `pass`.

assessor_question.description: Optional, and omitted unless needed. A yes/no question only the human assessor can settle, such as whether a deployed target is production. The finding's facts are verified, so it still counts and still fails `pass`.

root_cause.description: <repo-relative path>:<line> where the fixing change is made. Findings one change would fix share the value; it can differ from file and line. Optional so that reports from before 3.3.0 still validate; the prompt always emits it.

checked_requirements.description: Requirements actually evaluated against the scanned tree: the requirement text was read and the codebase searched for the control or violation it describes. Appearing in the reference is not 'checked'. A checked requirement in neither passed_requirements nor failed_requirements is inconclusive.

passed_requirements.description: Controls located and verified. Failing to find a violation is not verification.

failed_requirements.description: Exactly the asvs_requirement values of this report's findings, including those marked not_verifiable_in_code. Disjoint from passed_requirements.

sampled_requirements.description: Optional. Passed requirements whose evidence was sampled rather than read in full, keyed by requirement ID (e.g. V8.2.2) and mapped to 'sampled n of N: <method>'. Every key is in passed_requirements. Omitted when nothing was sampled.

not_applicable.description: IDs whose technology is absent: a chapter (V17), a section (V4.3), or a single requirement (V1.2.4) inside an otherwise applicable section. An entry covers every requirement beneath it, and none of those appears in checked_requirements.

not_applicable_reasons.description: One entry per not_applicable ID, keyed identically.

findings_addressed.description: Finding ids from this report's findings array.
